section.sectionSummaryBrief: Beyond elevating the shofar (delight) above, the shofar blast draws this delight into all worlds, including Asiyah, and on Shabbat this occurs without shofar because Shabbat itself draws delight into all worlds, even affecting the physical.
section.t: And behold, in addition to this, that through the shofar blast the shofar
(delight)
is made above
(in Zeir Anpin, etc.),
for what is above comes from you,
behold, through the shofar blast they draw the delight
(the aspect of shofar)
into all the worlds entirely,
even into the world of Asiyah.

And as we say in the Rosh Hashanah prayers, "And every deed shall know that You are its Doer, and every creature shall understand that You are its Creator, and all that has breath in its nostrils shall say," etc.,
and it is brought in the Siddur of the Arizal42
that these three expressions refer to the three worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah
[“Breath in its nostrils” refers to the world of Beriah,
“creature” to the world of Yetzirah, and “deed” to the world of Asiyah],
which are the totality of all the worlds,
and therefore on Rosh Hashanah we say these three expressions, because the drawing down of Rosh Hashanah is in all the worlds entirely,
even into the world of Asiyah.
And this that when Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbat we do not blow the shofar is because this matter that is accomplished through the shofar blast—
the drawing of delight into all worlds down to the lowest—
on Shabbat is accomplished from the aspect of Shabbat itself.
For it is known that the drawing down of Shabbat is in all the worlds,
even in Asiyah.
And as explained in several discourses
(and among them in the discourses of Rosh Hashanah)43
that the vitality of all the worlds,
even of the world of Asiyah,
on Shabbat is elevated above the vitality of weekdays.
For on weekdays the vitality of the worlds is from the letters of speech,
and on Shabbat their vitality is from the letters of thought.
Thus, Shabbat acts in all the worlds,
even in the physical world.
And this even effects a change in the nature of an ignoramus44,
that on Shabbat
(for by his nature)
he is unable to lie45.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: In the Temple they blew shofar even on Rosh Hashanah falling on Shabbat because the delight drawn through the shofar there was a higher aspect, beyond what Shabbat itself provides.
section.t: And that in the Temple they would blow the shofar even on Rosh Hashanah that fell on Shabbat
is because the aspect of delight
(the aspect of shofar)
that they drew through the shofar blast in the Temple was more elevated46.
That is, the delight that is drawn through the shofar blast in the provinces is the delight that Shabbat has from itself,
from the aspect that Shabbat is inherently sanctified,
and therefore on Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat they do not blow in the provinces,
but not so through the shofar blast in the Temple, they draw an aspect of delight that is more elevated,
which is not in Shabbat from itself
(and this is similar to what was explained above regarding "whoever delights in Shabbat,"
that there is an aspect of delight that is not in Shabbat from itself and is accomplished through the service of Israel),
and therefore in the Temple they would blow the shofar on Rosh Hashanah that fell on Shabbat.
For this aspect is higher than even the aspect of delight of "whoever delights in Shabbat"
(the service of Shabbat)47,
and is drawn only on Rosh Hashanah through the service of the shofar blast.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: There are two types of delight in mitzvos: the general delight in fulfilling G-d's will, and the specific delight unique to each mitzvah, which originates from the source of delights above revelation, explaining why the shofar's simple sound, being from that source, evokes awe rather than felt pleasure.
section.t: And the matter is
(as explained in the discourse there48),
that behold, in the delight of mitzvos there are two modes.
The first mode is the delight from having fulfilled the command of the Holy One, blessed be He,
"Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us,"
and this delight is equal in all mitzvos,
for since the will is equal in all mitzvos,
consequently the delight that comes from the will is equal in all of them.
And the second mode is the specific delight in each mitzvah,
for in each mitzvah there is a unique delight.
And it is explained in the discourse,
that the specific delight in each mitzvah is more elevated than the delight from the will that is equal in all mitzvos.
For this is a novel point in this discourse.
For elsewhere49
it is explained that the specific intention of each mitzvah is lower in level than the general intention,
and here it explains that the specific delight is more elevated50.
For the delight that is clothed in the will
(which is equal in all mitzvos)
is an aspect of the revelation of delight,
but not so the specific delight in each mitzvah, whose source is from the aspect of the source of delights, which is far above the aspect of the revelation of delight,
and from the aspect of the source of delights an illumination is drawn to each aspect specifically according to its level.
And based on this, it is explained there51
the matter of the shofar, that shofar is a term of delight
("He who gives words of beauty"),
for at first glance it is not understood,
for the matter of delight is specifically when there are several details,
and likewise with the delight in sound
(melody and musical instruments)
it is specifically when there is a combination of several sounds,
and since the shofar is a single sound,
how can it be said to contain delight?
And in practice we see,
that the sound of the shofar contains no delight,
and on the contrary it arouses trembling, as it is written52
"If a shofar is blown in the city, will the people not tremble?"53,
and likewise at the Giving of the Torah it is written54
"And the sound of the shofar was exceedingly strong, and all the people in the camp trembled," and it is written55
"And the people saw and moved and stood from afar,"
for from the greatest and most wondrous revelation in the sound of the shofar upon them, the effluence56
they were in a state of self-nullification
("and stood from afar"),
for trembling and self-nullification are the opposite of delight,
so how can it be said that shofar is a term and matter of delight?
And the explanation of this is
(as explained in the discourse there51),
that the shofar is delight because it is the aspect of the source of delights, which is above the aspect of the revelation of delight.
And therefore no feeling of delight at all is found in the sound of the shofar
(and on the contrary it casts trembling),
because it is above the aspect of revealed delight,
but rather it is from the aspect of the source of delights.
And from this aspect all specific delights are drawn.
For this is what "shofar" is a term for "improve your deeds,"
"your deeds" in the plural,
for through the shofar blast, improvement and delight appropriate to each particular deed are effected in every deed,
for the drawing from the aspect of the source of delights is
(as above)
specifically in a manner of division into details.
And this is also the connection of the shofar to the Giving of the Torah,
and as we say in the Musaf of Rosh Hashanah, "You revealed Yourself... to teach Your people Torah and mitzvos... and with the sound of the shofar You appeared to them,"
for at the Giving of the Torah there was the drawing down of Atzmus,
"I wrote and gave My very soul"57,
the drawing of the aspect of the source of delights, which is above the aspect of the revelation of delight,
and from this was subsequently drawn the delight in the Ten Commandments,
in each particular utterance
(at each and every utterance their souls flew away58)
the delight appropriate to that specific utterance,
and afterward this was drawn in greater particularity to "teach Your people Torah and mitzvos,"
in each and every mitzvah in particular.
